title: Portfolio
summary: This portfolio presents my résumé and projects while serving as a frontend work sample for interaction design, state management, accessibility, and content architecture. I built windows, folders, a Dock, and a terminal in the browser, then connected URLs, browser history, keyboard interaction, and preferences into one experience.

keyOutcome.value: Unified URL, History, and GUI state in one navigation model
keyOutcome.description: Shared links, refreshes, and browser Back restore the same project view.

intent.title: What I wanted to demonstrate
intent.description: I treated the portfolio itself as a frontend work sample. Beyond expressing an OS-style concept, I designed complex interaction to behave predictably in a real browser environment.

focus.interaction: OS-style interaction that feels natural inside the browser
focus.state: Screen state that survives shared URLs, Back navigation, and refreshes
focus.accessibility: A UI that supports keyboard exploration as well as mouse interaction

implementation.title: I designed interaction and state to remain predictable.
implementation.description: These four cases explain the frontend decisions that keep the visual concept and real usability working together.

navigation.title: I managed window state and URLs through one model.
navigation.context: Opening and moving between windows should not diverge from sharing a URL or using browser Back.
navigation.problem: When GUI window state and URL or browser history change separately, shared links and Back can show a different view.
navigation.decision: I correlated app IDs, URLs, parameters, and component props with types. A navigation planner calculates state and History API effects, while only the browser adapter calls the History API.
navigation.result: Window transitions, shared URLs, and browser history follow one state model. Structure and type checks catch missing IDs, URLs, loaders, and folder nodes when an app is added.
navigation.flow: User action → navigation planner → store command → browser adapter → URL, history, and GUI state

directory.title: I made the desktop and Projects folder one interaction model.
directory.context: Even on different surfaces, users should feel that they are selecting and opening items within the same OS.
directory.problem: Separate desktop and folder implementations easily diverge in selection, dragging, keyboard navigation, and resize behavior.
directory.decision: I defined an explicit folder tree that references GUI app IDs and rendered both surfaces with DirectorySurface. ResizeObserver tracks area changes and reclamps icon positions.
directory.result: Both surfaces use the same selection, focus, and drag rules. Icons remain in bounds after resizing and can be operated with a keyboard and move menu.
directory.flow: Desktop / Projects folder → DirectorySurface → DesktopItem → selection, focus, and drag

content.title: I separated content from user preferences.
content.context: Portfolio facts and the UI should remain consistent even when visitors change language, wallpaper, or Dock preferences.
content.problem: Korean and English content, UI labels, app metadata, and theme or wallpaper preferences can diverge when they live across many components.
content.decision: I separated reusable portfolio facts into a content model and UI labels into locale JSON. Server-safe metadata and client-side loaders are separate, while preferences persist in localStorage.
content.result: Career and Resume reuse the same experience, skill, and contact data. Localized content remains separate from UI labels, and language, wallpaper, and Dock preferences survive refreshes.
content.flow: Shared content → locale → GUI metadata → client loader → Career, Resume, and project views

accessibility.title: I made the OS-style UI navigable by keyboard.
accessibility.context: OS-style UI can easily depend on mouse dragging, but every visitor should be able to explore the portfolio.
accessibility.problem: When icons and windows only respond to mouse actions, keyboard users cannot easily find their current position or perform the same actions.
accessibility.decision: I made folders and icons operable with arrow keys, Enter, Escape, and a context menu. Focus position is separate from selection state, and a move menu provides an alternative to dragging.
accessibility.result: The visual concept remains intact while the interface can be explored without a mouse. Visitors can distinguish focus and selection as they follow the same project flow.
accessibility.flow: Roving focus → arrow-key navigation → Enter to open → Escape to clear selection → context menu to move

architecture.title: Navigation architecture for the OS-style portfolio
architecture.description: The terminal and GUI share the same app registry and content, while a navigation planner connects window state with browser history.
architecture.alt: Interactive portfolio architecture showing the terminal and GUI shell, navigation planner, GUI store, browser URL and History API, DirectorySurface, content, and preferences
architecture.caption: Window state and browser effects are separate, while repeated navigation interaction and content preferences are managed through shared boundaries.

otherContributions.title: Other Contributions
otherContributions.description: Beyond the featured navigation cases, localized content and keyboard accessibility are managed within the same product structure.

verification.title: Verification evidence
verification.description: I check structural contracts, browser navigation, and real interaction at separate levels so the OS-style UI keeps the same rules after changes.

structure.title: Application structure contracts
structure.description: Structure checks and unit tests keep app IDs, URLs, loaders, folder nodes, and localized title keys aligned.

navigation.title: URLs and browser navigation
navigation.description: Tests verify that shared-URL canonicalization, user navigation, Back, and popstate all follow the same navigation plan.

interaction.title: Real browser interaction
interaction.description: Playwright scenarios cover opening project windows, keeping windows in bounds, releasing DOM after close, and switching applications by keyboard.

result.title: I built a frontend work sample visitors can explore directly.
result.description: This project is not a shell for a portfolio. It is a frontend work sample that turns complex interaction into predictable state and structure for visitors to explore.
